Taking bugs_closed/298's explicitly unclaimed adjacent finding; 298's own cap defect is fixed, live and re-verified against live config today. who-owns.py checked for 298, 313 and 266: the two linker lanes are closed out and both files release this finding in terms; 266 is owned by the brochure_component_library lane and this change deliberately does NOT touch its seam.
rationale:
A discovery check has spent four months filing work items asking three different handlers to make RETIRED pages more reachable, and all three handlers correctly refuse. The producer is the only party that disagrees, and the disagreement is entirely internal to the platform.

THE INSTANCE. `findOrphanPagesSQL` (check_orphan_pages.go) constrains the page row with `datahelpers.PageHasShippedPredicateFor("p")` and NOTHING ELSE. That is the BUILD axis. The predicate family it comes from (datahelpers/links.go) states in terms that the build and lifecycle axes are separate and that each consumer must pair the arms its own question needs — this query pairs nothing, so an ARCHIVED page that shipped before it was retired is enumerated as an orphan and filed as work.

WHY IT IS A PRODUCER DEFECT AND NOT THREE HANDLER DEFECTS — the measurement that decided the shape. All three remedy paths ALREADY carry a lifecycle arm, each read first-hand 2026-08-22: needs_internal_links -> internal-linker, whose LIVE `load_target_page` step requires `p.status = 'active'`; nav_drift -> nav-updater, whose `navPageScopeSQL` is `status IN ('active','deployed','pending')`; orphan_blog_posts -> rerender-pages, whose `blogPostsQuery` is `p.status IN ('active','deployed')`. The producer is the sole outlier, so the fix belongs at the producer.

DAMAGE, MEASURED AND DISCONFIRMABLE. All 17 no-target `internal-linker` completions name an archived page — not a majority, all of them, with site_match true on every row. The fleet census runs the producer's own predicate verbatim and GROUPS BY pages.status, so it could have returned zero archived rows; it returns 34 archived pages being filed right now (15 needs_internal_links / 3 nav_drift / 16 blog). It recurs because idx_swi_dedup excludes terminal statuses, so the same keys have been re-raised 3-4 times since 2026-04-24. Second-order cost, and it is the expensive half: the no-op completions feed `writeWorkItem`'s two-strike ladder (load_work_item_actions.go:1468-1504, read first-hand), which rewrites the item `unresolved` — TERMINAL and undispatchable. bugs_closed/313 already established this is what parked the linker's queue, and 15 of those 20 parked items name an ACTIVE page. So the defect retires legitimate work as collateral.

THE CLASS. Reading the SQL of all 71 non-test files in discovery_checks: 18 checks can select an archived page AND route it at a handler. It is an ADOPTION GAP, not eighteen independent mistakes — only 3 files call PageWantedLivePredicateFor; the rest hand-spell it four ways, and two of those spellings do nothing at all. `COALESCE(p.status,'') <> 'deleted'` (check_sectionless_pages, priority 90, routes page-build-handler) excludes NO ROW, because pages.status has exactly two live values, active 759 / archived 65. `p.status IN ('active','deployed')` works only by accident — `deployed` is a build_status value. Both READ as lifecycle filters.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, AND THE PRECEDENT THAT SAYS SO. This is not 'audits should skip archived pages'. bugs_open/266's note of 2026-08-14 from the bugfix_168 lane warns against exactly that: an archived page can still serve 200 to the public, so a check that only OBSERVES is right to look at it, and check_unverified_claims has a MUTATION TEST defending precisely that behaviour. The discriminator is what the finding's REMEDY does. All three of check_orphan_pages' remedies make the page more reachable, and the correct action on a retired page that is still serving is retraction (bugs_closed/098), never re-linking. This is why the posture registry has FOUR values and not two: a two-valued guard would have pushed check_unverified_claims' nuanced predicate back into hand-spelling, which is the disease.

A SHARED-SEAM GUARD WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, on evidence. bugs_open/266 fixed its own four-producer problem at the one seam every producer passes through, and that seam exists here too and is genuinely singular (discovery_checks.go:238-264, verified first-hand). Rejected for three reasons: (1) the right answer differs per check, so a seam-level archived filter would break check_unverified_claims; (2) 266's state admits no exceptions ('archived' = nothing may deploy this) and this one does; (3) it would not even work — the seam sees only item.pageID, and check_orphan_pages does not set PageID at all, embedding the id in spec JSON as TEXT. Recorded as fix candidate C in the bug file rather than silently dropped.

THE GUARD IS MUTATION-PROVEN, AND IT TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS. This is submitted as evidence about the guard, not as colour. v1 read the whole file, so the arm's own explanatory COMMENT satisfied it. v2 stripped comments by hand and read the `/*` inside `req.Header.Set("Accept", "*/*")` as a block-comment opener, discarding the rest of two files and failing them while correctly armed — and its header claimed its only weakness was UNDER-stripping, 'which could only ever cause a false PASS', so the stated limit was wrong about its own direction. v3 uses go/scanner and binds the needle to a DECLARED PAGES ALIAS, because an unqualified `status = 'active'` is satisfied by the `site_nav_items sni` join nearly every check here carries — the same false-clean reading a grep-count gave while filing this bug. Final proof, with the decoys deliberately left in: deleting the arm from check_orphan_pages.go fails the test while the file still contains the string in a comment AND twice on the nav join; breaking the shared toolEligibilityWhere fragment fails its own test. Both missteps are in WRONG_CALLS.

THE ALLOW-LIST LANDMINE IS THE MAIN DESIGN RISK AND IS ANSWERED STRUCTURALLY. LANDMINES records that a declared key silences the detector it was written for, and COMPONENT_WRITE_ALLOWED's own note says adding a known gap 'converts a live debt into a false all-clear'. Defences: KnownGap is a DISTINCT value from Observes, not a pass; every KnownGap Reason must name bugs_open/356 (enforced by a test); and the backlog test PRINTS the count, so 23 gaps read as 23 gaps rather than as silence. Fixing one is a one-line change plus moving the entry to Armed, at which point the assertion starts enforcing it.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: fixing the other 17 routing gaps in this change (each needs its own judgement about what its remedy does — that is the point of the registry, and batching them would be exactly the unreviewed sweep this bug is about); sweeping the existing rows (RFC_006 — a one-off deletion is not a class fix, and they self-heal once the producer stops re-raising them); setting WorkItemSpec.PageID on the three orphan specs (real, small, independent — recorded as candidate E for its own ticket); building an 'archived and still serving' detector (none exists anywhere in the package [MEASURED]; this change neither creates nor closes that gap, and the bug file says so).

edits.rationale: The instance fix, and the only behaviour change in this submission. Adds the LIFECYCLE arm beside the existing BUILD arm so the producer agrees with all three of its own remedy paths. The comment block is the load-bearing half of the edit: it records WHY the arm belongs here (what the three remedies do) and warns in terms against generalising it into 'audits should skip archived pages', which is bugs_open/266's documented opposite error.

The class closer, modelled on this package's existing verifier_coverage_test.go / handler_coverage_test.go idiom (same sensor+ratchet shape) because a second, differently-shaped list is the drift this bug is about. Four postures rather than two, because check_unverified_claims runs a legitimate NUANCED predicate that a binary guard could not express — and forcing it back to hand-spelling would reproduce the adoption gap. Keyed by FILE because that is what an author adds; a file with mixed queries records the WEAKEST posture and names the weak query.

The entry states the boundary explicitly (this is NOT a blanket archived filter) and carries the three-attempt mutation story as its landmine, which is the transferable part.
